title: SQL Injection in services.store.find_items (parameter 'category')
label: confirmed

code_findings.title: SQL injection: request data reaches execute() through an f-string

code.snippet:
conn = get_db()
    rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM items WHERE category = '{category}'").fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]

runtime.request:
GET /api/items?category=books%27 HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
User-Agent: FlowStopper-dast
Accept: */*
runtime.response_excerpt:
HTTP/1.1 500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

...sqlite3.OperationalError: unrecognized token: "'books''"...
runtime.evidence: Appending a quote to 'category' produced 'sqlite3.OperationalError: unrecognized token'; the baseline response has no SQL error.

primary_code.snippet:
conn = get_db()
    rows = conn.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM items WHERE category = '{category}'").fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]

primary_runtime.request:
GET /api/items?category=books%27 HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
User-Agent: FlowStopper-dast
Accept: */*
primary_runtime.response_excerpt:
HTTP/1.1 500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

...sqlite3.OperationalError: unrecognized token: "'books''"...
primary_runtime.evidence: Appending a quote to 'category' produced 'sqlite3.OperationalError: unrecognized token'; the baseline response has no SQL error.

reasons.detail: SAST CWE-89 and DAST CWE-89 are in the same family (sqli)
taint flow originates at handler views.catalog.list_items for route GET /api/items (full taint chain, +0.05 specificity)
DAST method GET == route method GET

fix:
What is wrong: services.store.find_items (services/store.py:9) puts the request parameter 'category' into an SQL statement instead of binding it as a parameter, so the input can change the query itself.

Minimal fix:
```python
# bind the value as a parameter; never put it inside the SQL text
cur.execute("SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE column_name = ?", (category,))
```

Prevention: Use parameterised queries or an ORM everywhere, and never build SQL with f-strings, % or +.

title: Hard-coded credential in settings.py (SECRET_KEY)
label: code_only
fix:
What is wrong: settings.py contains a hard-coded credential (SECRET_KEY), so anyone who can read the source can use it.

Minimal fix:
```python
import os
SECRET_KEY = os.environ["SECRET_KEY"]  # set it in the environment or a secret manager
```

Prevention: Keep secrets out of source control, rotate the exposed value now, and run a secret scanner in CI.

title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header (host-wide)
label: runtime_only

runtime.request:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
User-Agent: FlowStopper-dast
Accept: */*
runtime.response_excerpt:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 512
runtime.evidence: No Content-Security-Policy header on 5 of 5 sampled paths: /, /api/items, /api/ping, /api/report, /search

primary_runtime.request:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
User-Agent: FlowStopper-dast
Accept: */*
primary_runtime.response_excerpt:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 512
primary_runtime.evidence: No Content-Security-Policy header on 5 of 5 sampled paths: /, /api/items, /api/ping, /api/report, /search

fix:
What is wrong: Responses miss a browser security header (Missing Content-Security-Policy header), so the browser does not apply that protection.

Minimal fix:
```python
@app.after_request
def add_security_headers(resp):
    resp.headers.setdefault("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
    resp.headers.setdefault("Content-Security-Policy", "default-src 'self'")
    resp.headers.setdefault("Referrer-Policy", "strict-origin-when-cross-origin")
    return resp
```

Prevention: Set security headers once, in middleware or the reverse proxy, so every response gets them.

title: OS Command Injection in services.net.ping_host (suppressed)
label: code_only

code_findings.title: Command execution with request data (list form, no shell)

fix:
What is wrong: services.net.ping_host (services/net.py:21) passes the request parameter 'host' to a shell, so characters such as ; | or $( ) run extra commands.

Minimal fix:
```python
import subprocess
# argument list, no shell: the value is one argument, never parsed by a shell
subprocess.run(["program", "--option", host], shell=False, check=True, timeout=10)
# if a shell string is unavoidable: shlex.quote(value)
```

Prevention: Call programs with an argument list and shell=False, and check the value against an allow-list (for example a strict regex) first.
